decision: O4: 3 parallel band lanes into the VM (existing rb0..rb2 face, PAR_RB=1) + row-compressed slots (NS = port bframe active prefix) + one-burst band lag
why: cheapest structure <= 5 % e2e: same serializer banks/FF (-27 FF/band), no new VM port or face bits (rb face already 3 x 551 b, cut unchanged), VM gains a per-bank 3-lane AND-OR (~80 banks x 548 b AO222, ~0.006 mm2 est.); O3 (3 lanes, 8 slots) 5.11 %, O5 (2 lanes) 5.32 %, O2 (1 lane compressed) 9.47 % exceed 5 %; O6 (6 lanes wide beats) 0.26 % but doubles the rb face (3,306 b) and needs 6 rows/edge on 16-bank replicas
bench_convention: tb_vmwb edge index (one rq register after the ports, +1 vs tb_sertrade); model wb_calendar.py reproduces every landing (pos/base/o3) exactly after the +1
mutant_note: vpmut1 PC11 passes: PC11 (mmode lane-vector writes) bands 1 and 2 carry identical data words in this stimulus; the mutant is rejected on PC1/12/16/20
pc11: included: 8 captures, 192 we rows (128 mask-0), NS 8; charged to attn_kv in the ledger
checks: every we row read back from the real VM (svr row read, 13 edges) lane-by-lane vs the port-order golden image
land_cnt == bursts and each end beat only after all rows of bursts <= n
serializer/issuer/VM faults 0 (VM static_conflict covers lane/lane, lane/SU, lane/skid)
row law of the compiler == actual 24-port RTL rows (rows/*.log)
bank-conflict-free proof mod 16 and mod 64 for every edge (calendar.json)
limits: component scope: one rank (24 ports, soft-mul variant of the same port source), one ME op per run; no physical views; die relays fold into TRAIN_EDGES (die-assigned, -1 refuses)
VM conflict-freedom against other writers (SU/seq/mx/attention rows) remains the layer calendar's duty (static_conflict faults)
